title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Asha Kapoor
commits: introduce streaming lifecycle control events and headers
server: add idle/response timeout heuristics and metrics
stream: implement client-cancel, disconnect handling and resume token plumbing
compat: OpenAI compatibility layer - surface cancel/disconnect semantics
tests: add unit and integration tests for lifecycle transitions
docs: API surface and migration notes
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints were sensitive to client-initiated cancels and abrupt disconnects which left in-flight sessions consuming GPU KV cache and prevented clean resume or fair scheduling. This PR introduces explicit lifecycle control events and server-side timeout heuristics to make streaming stable and predictable across SSE and WebSocket transports, and aligns behavior with our OpenAI compatibility layer. What this changes: 1) protocol-level lifecycle events: CLIENT_CANCEL, CLIENT_DISCONNECT, SERVER_TIMEOUT, RESUME_AVAILABLE surfaced over SSE and WS as structured control frames; 2) session manager tracks session state and resume tokens; short-lived resume tokens are issued for reconnects and validated against resume_store; 3) server timeouts: idle and response timeouts are applied per-session with exponential backoff and metric hooks so we can detect noisy clients and protect GPUs; 4) OpenAI compat: /v1/streams now returns the same cancel/disconnect semantics and status codes expected by popular clients; 5) SDKs: Python/TS helpers to surface client cancel and reconnect workflows; 6) Observability: new metrics and traces for lifecycle transitions, resume success/failure, and timeout-induced cancellations. Checklist: - Implementation (service + protocol + compat) - Docs (api/docs/streaming_lifecycle.md) - Unit tests and integration tests added - Performance: microbenchmarks and canary run for 72h - Migration notes included for consumers. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged for clients that don't opt into resume; resume tokens are opt-in and expire quickly. Rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_lifecycle; gradual rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor metrics, then 100%.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Architecturally this looks good. Two asks: add a metric for 'resume_token_issued' with cardinality limits, and make the token TTL configurable via runtime config.
Asha Kapoor: Added resume_token_issued metric and wired TTL to runtime config (defaults to 60s). See commit 'server: add resume TTL config'.
Devon Chen: Integration tests are flaky on CI (intermittent websocket reconnect failure). Suggest making test wait for resume token to be acknowledged before sending data.
Asha Kapoor: Updated integration test to wait for RESUME_AVAILABLE control frame and added a retry/assertion; reran CI.
Priya Nair: OpenAI compatibility note: we should return HTTP 499 for client cancels from the compat layer to match common client expectations.
Asha Kapoor: Compat layer now maps client cancel to 499 for streaming endpoints; documented in streaming_lifecycle.md.
release_notes: Adds streaming lifecycle controls (client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, server-side timeouts) with OpenAI-compat behavior. Feature gated; rollout planned with canary. SDK helper updates included.
